solves.reasoning: (A) finalize — Britain decided to finalize the border in 1899; initiate means start, but the passage uses 'finalize'. (B) arbitrarily — the border 'arbitrarily tore through'; deliberately (의도적으로) implies careful planning, but the passage says 'arbitrarily' (무작위로). (C) desirable — Egypt wanted to 'keep the desirable Hala'ib'; undesirable contradicts why Egypt would fight for it.

(A) colonial — the passage says 'In colonial fashion'; modern contradicts the 1899 British Empire context. (B) reflect — 'drew a new line to reflect tribal territories'; ignore contradicts the purpose. (C) long-standing — the conflict is described as 'long-standing'; recently emerged contradicts the 1899-1902 historical backdrop.

(A) tribal — 'new line to reflect tribal territories'; national contradicts the purpose (they drew it specifically to address tribal, not national, boundaries). (B) intersecting — 'two intersecting lines'; parallel lines wouldn't create two distinct areas. (C) refuse — 'both countries refuse to claim Bir Tawil'; agree would make the situation normal, not strange.

② 'coastal' is wrong: Bir Tawil is described as 'an empty, landlocked patch of desert' — landlocked means no coast. Coastal directly contradicts this. (The Hala'ib Triangle is the coastal area, not Bir Tawil.)

② 'reluctantly' is wrong: Egypt 'understandably claimed' the border — understandably implies naturally/logically motivated action. Reluctantly (마지못해) contradicts this motivation — Egypt was eager to claim Hala'ib, not reluctant.

③ 'acquiring' is wrong: passage says 'it would mean giving up a greater prize' — both countries refuse to claim Bir Tawil because claiming it means giving up, not acquiring, the greater prize (Hala'ib).

Blank: 'this new international border ___ tore through local tribes'. Using a straight geographic line ignores local realities = arbitrarily (임의적으로). Precisely/carefully/peacefully don't match the context of colonial indifference.
Blank: 'these two ___ lines'. Two different lines that cross each other = intersecting (교차하는). Parallel (평행한) lines don't create two new areas. Identical/vanishing don't fit.

Blank: 'the large, ___ coastal area called the Hala'ib Triangle'. The contrast is with 'empty, landlocked' Bir Tawil. Hala'ib is desirable and liveable = inhabitable (거주 가능한). Deserted/barren/landlocked all describe Bir Tawil, not Hala'ib.
finalize = settle (확정하다/결정짓다). Cancel (취소), postpone (연기), dispute (분쟁) are all wrong. To finalize a border = to settle/conclude it definitively.
reflect (반영하다) = represent (나타내다/반영하다). Distort (왜곡), conceal (숨기다), overlook (간과하다) are all wrong. 'Drew a new line to reflect tribal territories' = to represent/account for the tribal areas.
conflict = dispute (분쟁). Agreement (협정), alliance (동맹), negotiation (협상) are all peaceful/cooperative — opposite of conflict. Dispute best matches the contentious border claim.
empty (비어있는)의 반의어 = occupied (점유된/가득 찬). Vacant/hollow are synonyms of empty. Barren is also similar (황량한). Occupied is the antonym.
refuse (거부하다)의 반의어 = consent (동의하다/수락하다). Decline/reject/deny are all synonyms of refuse. Consent (허락/동의) is the direct antonym.

(A) 'the conveniently straight line of the twenty-second parallel of latitude' — line = (경계) 선 (geographic boundary line). (B) 'wait in line until your number is called' — line = (대기) 줄. So (A)경계선 - (B)대기줄 = choice 1.
'Relating to a country or system that controls another country' = colonial (식민지의). Tribal (부족의), international (국제적인), coastal (해안의) don't match this definition of colonial power.
commune → communities (plural noun). 'Tore through local tribes and communities' — commune as a noun becomes community (공동체), plural = communities.
inhabit → inhabitable (adjective). 'The large, inhabitable coastal area' — inhabit (거주하다) → inhabitable (거주 가능한), adjective form used to modify 'coastal area'.

Both Egypt and Sudan blank the original/new border for the same reason: to keep Hala'ib. The common verb = claimed (주장했다). Denied/abandoned/rejected are all opposite to what Egypt and Sudan were doing.

Blank: 'it would mean giving up a greater ___'. Both countries refuse Bir Tawil because claiming it means losing Hala'ib = prize (상/더 큰 것). Burden (부담), territory (영토), challenge (도전) don't fit the context of strategic sacrifice.
